answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the ridge gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 100 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the river ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the opal review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
